standard.title: Adverb and prepositional phrases
standard.description: understand how adverb groups/phrases and prepositional phrases work in different ways to provide circumstantial details about an activity
standard.prior_knowledge: Students understand how different verb types and tense work in clauses (AC9E3LA07, AC9E3LA08). They have not yet examined how adverb groups/phrases and prepositional phrases provide circumstantial details of time, place, manner and cause around activities.
standard.progression_endpoint: Students can identify adverb groups/phrases and prepositional phrases in sentences, classify the type of circumstantial detail each provides (time, place, manner, cause), and explain how these phrases add precision to descriptions of activities.

nodes.label: Circumstantial details — what, when, where, how
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify that sentences can include additional information about the circumstances surrounding an activity — when it happened, where, how and why.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify at least two different types of circumstantial detail in a provided sentence (e.g. time and place) and name what question each answers.
nodes.typical_width: Identify all four types of circumstantial detail — time, place, manner, cause — across a range of sentences and explain how each adds precision to the description of an activity.
wider: Compare how circumstantial detail is used differently in narrative (for atmosphere and pace) versus scientific description (for precision and replicability)
Examine how removing circumstantial phrases changes the meaning and specificity of a sentence across different text types
nodes.hinge_reason: Identifying adverb and prepositional phrases in N2 and N3 requires students to know what type of circumstantial detail they are providing — without N1's time/place/manner/cause framework, classification in N2 and N3 is impossible.

response_modes.reason: Circumstantial detail types appear across narrative and factual texts with different distributions — multiple contexts help students see how each type functions differently across purposes, before they encounter them as adverb and prepositional phrases.

success_criteria: Can identify at least three types of circumstantial detail in a sentence and name the question each answers (when? where? how?)
Can explain that circumstantial phrases add detail to the main activity without changing what the activity is

nodes.label: Adverb groups and phrases
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify adverb groups and adverb phrases in sentences and explain what circumstantial detail each provides.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify an adverb group or phrase in a sentence and name the type of circumstantial information it provides.
nodes.typical_width: Identify adverb groups and phrases of time, place, manner and cause across texts, noting how they differ from single adverbs and explaining what each adds to the activity described.
wider: Collect adverb phrases from texts in different subject areas and analyse what types of circumstantial information are most common in each (e.g. manner in science descriptions, time in recounts)
Create sentences using adverb phrases in different positions (initial, medial, final) and evaluate how placement changes emphasis

response_modes.reason: Students readily identify single adverbs but often miss adverb phrases (e.g. 'with great care', 'in the early morning'). Recognition of phrases rather than single words requires repeated practice.

success_criteria: Can identify an adverb phrase (not just a single adverb) in a sentence
Can name what type of circumstance the phrase provides

nodes.label: Prepositional phrases
nodes.progression_checkpoint: Students can identify prepositional phrases and explain the circumstantial detail each provides about an activity.
nodes.minimum_width: Identify a prepositional phrase in a sentence and explain what circumstantial detail it adds (e.g. place, time).
nodes.typical_width: Identify prepositional phrases providing different circumstantial details across texts — locative (from the chair, into the forest), temporal (at midnight, during the storm), manner (with a smile, in silence) — and explain what each adds to the activity.
wider: Compare prepositional phrase use in literary and factual texts — how do authors use prepositional phrases for atmosphere versus precision?
Examine how stacking multiple prepositional phrases in one sentence (as in the elaboration example) builds richly circumstantiated description

response_modes.reason: Prepositional phrase repertoire is built through encountering many examples across literary and factual texts — accumulation enables the stacked-phrase authorial control that the wider tier describes.

nodes.width_opportunity_reason: The use of stacked prepositional phrases for richly circumstantiated description — as in the example 'At midnight he rose slowly from the chair and went upstairs' — is a genuinely rich area for writers. Wider engagement builds authorial control.
success_criteria: Can identify a prepositional phrase and name the preposition that begins it
Can explain what circumstantial information the phrase provides
